top_news.title: Human Preference aligned Tabular Similarity
top_news.dek: Researchers argue that standard tabular embedding metrics fail to capture human preference, necessitating new alignment methods for similarity search.
top_news.brief: Task-agnostic tabular embeddings are widely used in business systems like PLM, but current approaches prioritize prediction over human-aligned similarity. The authors suggest that downstream metrics are insufficient for evaluating trustworthiness in similarity search, proposing a shift toward human-preference alignment.

top_news.title: Document-borne AI worms can self-propagate through Copilot for Word
top_news.dek: A security analysis reveals vulnerabilities in Microsoft Copilot for Word that could allow for self-propagating AI worms.
top_news.brief: The research, conducted in coordination with Microsoft's Security Response Center, details how AI-driven document processing could be exploited to create self-propagating malicious code. The findings highlight risks associated with context-aware AI agents in office productivity software.

top_news.title: Configuring Dedicated Model Inference
top_news.dek: Together AI details its resource model for dedicated inference, emphasizing capacity-aware routing across endpoints and deployments.
top_news.brief: The platform's architecture separates endpoints, deployments, and configurations to enable flexible traffic management. By using capacity-aware routing rather than fixed percentages, the system supports A/B testing, shadow deployments, and zero-downtime updates.

top_news.title: OpenAI open-sources Codex Security CLI to help developers find and fix vulnerabilities from the command line
top_news.dek: OpenAI has open-sourced its internal security CLI, now called Codex Security CLI, to automate vulnerability detection and remediation.
top_news.brief: Formerly known as Aardvark, the tool is designed to scan code repositories and suggest fixes for security flaws. It is released under the Apache 2.0 license and aims to help developers address vulnerabilities directly from the command line.
top_news.image_alt: Command line interface showing security scan results

top_news.title: Liquid AI Releases LFM2.5-Encoder-230M and LFM2.5-Encoder-350M: Bidirectional Encoders That Stay Fast at 8K Context on CPU
top_news.dek: Liquid AI has launched LFM2.5-Encoder models, offering efficient bidirectional encoding with 8K context support for CPU-based environments.
top_news.brief: The 230M and 350M parameter models are built on the LFM2 hybrid backbone and are optimized for tasks like intent routing and PII detection. The 230M variant can process an 8K-token forward pass on a CPU in approximately 28 seconds.
top_news.image_alt: Performance chart of Liquid AI encoders

primary.title: TimeCapsule: Generative Hallucination as a Method for Historical Sensemaking
primary.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are temporally overexposed: trained on vast contemporary corpora, they encode present-day concepts that make them unreliable narrators of the past. We present TimeCapsule, a 1.2B-parameter LLaMA-style causal model trained exclusively on Victorian texts (1800-1875) as an epistemologically isolated generative archive. Quantitative evaluation shows a 45.4% perplexity reduction over a GPT-2 baseline on held-out Victorian prose, while larger contemporary causal models achieve lower raw perplexity through broader pretraining but lack temporal isolation. primary.title: The Orchestrator's Tax
primary.summary: Subagents get justified by time saved and parallel execution, but Rahul Garg explains that's not what matters most. Every token in the orchestrator's context is competing for its attention, and the real value of a subagent is what it keeps out of that context. Subagents should be treated as a tool for protecting the orchestrator's working memory, offloading reasoning it doesn't need to hold onto. Doing this well means giving the orchestrator explicit ground rules for when and how to delegate. more…

primary.title: Microsoft AI Releases MAI-Cyber-1-Flash: A 5B-Active-Parameter Cyber Model That Pushes MDASH to 95.95% on CyberGym
primary.summary: Microsoft AI has released MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, its first model built specifically for cyber defense. It is a 137B total, 5B active sparse MoE fine-tune of MAI-Code-1-Flash with a 256k context window. The model does not ship as a standalone endpoint — it runs inside MDASH, Microsoft's multi-model agentic scanning harness, where it handles up to 90% of tasks and pushes the system to 95.95% on CyberGym.
